description:
THE HEADLINE FIX FOR 'I GET TACKLED AND THEN I CAN'T DO ANYTHING'. ONE BYTE. Test this FIRST and on its own.

THE PROBLEM, IN ONE SENTENCE. When you are knocked into a stagger, the engine asks the stagger 'may this request interrupt you?' and answers from a cancel keyframe baked into the animation. Every request in the game uses the FIRST cancel keyframe - Trap, Tackle, Block, Reaction, kicks. Exactly ONE request is singled out and routed to the LAST cancel keyframe instead: kind 4, Dribble, which is 'keep running with the ball'. So the single thing you actually want after being barged - carry on with it, turn back into the man - is the one thing the game makes you wait to the end of the animation for.

WHAT CHANGES. match::anime::action::Stagger::vf14 (0x143f00de0). At 0x143f00ef6 the code does 'cmp r14d,4 / jne 0x143f00f40'. The equal path fetches the LAST channel-5 cancel key (index = count-1), or the channel-3 END key when the motion has only one cancel key. The not-equal path is the generic first-key path everything else uses. This pack turns that 'jne' into an unconditional 'jmp' so Dribble falls through to the generic path. One byte, same length, no pool cell touched, no new code.

MEASURED EFFECT (a-EMULATED, this pass, end to end through the REAL requester). Frame at which the request is allowed to start, current action = Stagger, synthetic motion with cancel keys at frames 16/32/48 and the end key at 64:
    motion layout            stock   THIS PACK
    3 cancel keys 16/32/48    48       16      (3.0x earlier)
    1 cancel key  16          64       16      (4.0x earlier)
    2 cancel keys 8/40        40        8      (5.0x earlier)
    no cancel key             64        4      (16x earlier)
Trap is unchanged at 16 in every layout - this pack only moves Dribble onto the same footing as everything else.

HOW IT KEEPS THE WEIGHT. This does NOT open the gate. Swept frame by frame with the byte applied, Dribble out of a stagger is still refused at frames 0, 4, 8, 12 and 15, and first starts at 16. The stagger animation is not shortened, not scaled and not skipped - it plays at full length with full visual weight. You simply stop being a passenger a third of the way through instead of at the end. Contact still costs you a step; it stops costing you the whole animation.

EVIDENCE.
  a-EMULATED - the whole chain on the game's own bytes under Unicorn: 0x143eb4f40 (the requester) -> Dribble::vf2 0x143f99eb0 -> Stagger::vf14 0x143f00de0 -> the action starter 0x143eb4fd0, against a synthetic action registry and MbInfoManager. Harness tools/emu_contact_request.py, output build/emu_contact_request_proof.txt sections 2, 6 and 7.
  a-EMULATED - the requester really is the caller of vf2: 0x143eb4fad-0x143eb4fbc is 'mov rcx,[rax] / mov r8,[rcx+0x10] / mov rcx,rax / call r8 / test al,al / jne -> start'. Vtable slot 2 is at offset 0x10. This closes the question every earlier pass left open.
  b-DISASSEMBLY - the kind==4 branch at 0x143f00ef6 and the last-key fetch at 0x143f00f00-0x143f00f3e.
  NOT CLAIMED - the absolute length of the stock lock in milliseconds. The raw keyframes live in cpk_dat/common/anime/Mbinfo/bin/CancelData.bin, not in the exe, so every frame number above is from a synthetic motion table fed to the real code. The RATIO (last key vs first key) is exact; the seconds are not known.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE - your stick-controlled player, your AI team-mates and the CPU. Stagger::vf14 reads only the motion id, the contact sub-kind byte, the requested kind and the current frame. There is no controlled-player test, no team test and no attribute read anywhere in the function, so this is not a one-sided buff. Expect CPU ball carriers to ride challenges better too. That is correct for realism and should not be sold as a player advantage.

WHAT YOU SHOULD SEE IN ONE MATCH. Get shoulder-barged or clipped while carrying the ball in midfield. Stock, you watch the stumble finish and the defender takes it. With this, you should be able to push the ball on and keep the duel alive while still visibly stumbling.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT. If after two halves a knocked player still feels like he cannot touch the ball until the animation finishes, then either the staggers you are running into are the heavy motions with a different keyframe layout, or the request your stick makes is not Dribble. In that case go to contact-move-out-of-stagger.json next, which covers the case where you have LOST the ball.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO FAR. Players skating out of collisions - the knock plays but the man is already moving normally under it, so contact reads as cosmetic. If you see that, revert; do NOT reach for the scale lever as well.

COLLISIONS. Site 0x143f00efa verified byte-identical between the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE this pass (both 75). Does not overlap any of the 26 applied specs. DO NOT apply this together with contact-cancel-window-x2.json - they are different mechanisms on the same quantity and stack multiplicatively (emulated: stock 48, this pack 16, the scale pack 24, BOTH 8 - a 6x change you will not be able to attribute).

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS: NONE. This pack adds no challenge and no collision. The foul scorer 0x143d88fe0 and its 40/60 thresholds and 80/110 card lines are untouched.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/contact-dribble-cancel-early.json

patches.name: Stagger::vf14 - Dribble stops being routed to the LAST cancel keyframe
patches.note: 'jne 0x143f00f40' -> 'jmp 0x143f00f40' at the 'cmp r14d,4' (requested kind == Dribble) test inside match::anime::action::Stagger::vf14 (0x143f00de0). The equal path computed idx = count(channel-5 keys) - 1 (the LAST cancel key) and fell back to the channel-3 END key when there was only one; the not-equal path is the generic idx = 0 path that Trap, Tackle, Block and Reaction already use. Private conditional-branch opcode byte, same instruction length, no pool cell read or written.
